summary:
## Creating a Custom Medusa Monster High Doll

This document outlines the key steps and materials used to transform a standard Monster High doll into a unique Medusa-inspired creation, featuring a sculpted snake wig and tail.

### Key Materials
- **Doll**: A secondhand Monster High doll (in this case, a broken one).
- **Sculpting**: **Polymer clay** and **liquid polymer clay** for the wig and tail. **Air-dry clay** for final assembly.
- **Face Repaint**: **Acetone** nail polish remover, **Mr. Super Clear** sealant, **watercolor pencils**, **chalk pastels**, and **alcohol ink**.
- **Finishing**: **Acrylic paint**, **gold alcohol ink**, **water-based glaze**, rhinestones, and copper wire.

### Sculpting the Custom Parts

#### Snake Hair Wig
1.  **Create a Base**: Cover the doll's head in **tin foil** to protect it.
2.  **Form the Wig Cap**: Apply a thin sheet of **polymer clay** over the tin foil to create a cap.
3.  **Partial Curing**: Use a **hairdryer** to gently heat-set the surface of the clay, making it firm enough to work on without deforming.
4.  **Add Snakes**: Sculpt individual snakes and attach them to the cap using **liquid polymer clay**.
5.  **Bake**: After another gentle pass with the hairdryer, carefully remove the entire wig piece from the doll's head and bake it according to the polymer clay package instructions.

> [!NOTE]
> Covering the doll's body in tin foil allows you to arrange the snakes over her shoulders without the raw clay touching and potentially damaging the plastic.

#### Snake Tail
1.  **Prepare the Doll**: Remove the doll's legs.
2.  **Form the Tail**: Sculpt a large tail shape from **polymer clay** around the doll's lower torso, which is protected by **tin foil**.
3.  **Shape and Bake**: Shape the base of the tail so the doll can stand or sit upright. Carefully remove the doll and bake the tail.

### The Face Repaint Process
1.  **Preparation**: Remove the factory paint with **acetone**. Apply a base coat of **Mr. Super Clear** to create a matte, toothy surface for the art supplies.
2.  **First Layer**: Sketch the eyes and brows. A **green chalk pastel** is used to give the skin a greenish undertone.
3.  **Layering and Sealing**: Build up color and shading in layers. Spray with **Mr. Super Clear** between each layer to fix the work and prevent smudging.
4.  **Shading for Depth**: Use **black chalk pastel** in the corners of the eyes to create a rounded effect and **dark brown pastel** to deepen facial contours.
5.  **Highlights**: Use a light skin-toned pencil for subtle highlights and a wet white pencil for sharp, final highlights in the eyes.

### Assembly and Finishing

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Use **air-dry clay** to connect the baked polymer clay tail to the plastic doll body. The doll itself cannot be baked, so oven-bake clay cannot be used for the final assembly.

- **Connect the Tail**: Use air-dry clay to create a smooth transition from the doll's torso to the sculpted tail. Smooth it with water and let it dry completely.
- **Paint**: Paint the tail and wig using **acrylic paints**.
- **Details**: Attach the gold-painted top, add wire cuffs, apply a **water-based glaze** for gloss on the lips, and glue **rhinestones** for the snakes' eyes.
transcription:
## Introduction to the Medusa Doll Project

Hi guys, in today's video we'll be making this Medusa inspired doll repaint. I've been thinking about doing this type of doll for a while, so I was really happy when some of you guys started requesting it.

I decided on giving Medusa a snake tail as well as snake hair, but obviously that's up to you. Let's get started on this project.

## Creating a Polymer Clay Wig Cap

I'll be using this Cleo doll which I'd bought secondhand online. When I first received it, I started by removing the hair because it was really tangled and gross, but then I realized that one of the legs was actually broken. I still kept the doll, thinking that it might be good for a character that didn't need its legs, for instance Medusa, so that's why we're using it.

Last thing, we're gonna make a new hair for this. I took a piece of tin foil, covered the head completely, then I took some polymer clay, rolled it out in a thin sheet, and then spread this on top of the head to create a polymer clay wig cap of sorts.

## Sculpting the Snake Hair

Once I had the hair portion covered, then I took my beat-up old hair dryer and I used the heat of this to set the surface, to harden the clay just a bit so I could still work on it without misshaping it. Then you want to form the snakes from polymer clay. Using a bit of liquid clay to stick the snakes on, you want to start adding them to the wig cap.

## Baking the Snake Wig

I covered the rest of the doll in tin foil too so I could arrange the snake onto her body without getting it in contact with the actual plastic of the doll. Once I had all the snakes attached and arranged, I used the hair dryer again to gently set them so I could slide the doll's head out from under the tin foil and then carefully bake it completely according to package instructions.

## Sculpting the Polymer Clay Snake Tail

Once baked, you can remove the tin foil and try it on your doll, and here's how it looks. Put it aside for now. Next, we want to remove the broken leg as well as the bottom part of the other leg. Then I used a few pieces of masking tape to stick the legs together.

Now you want to take a big chunk of polymer clay and start forming the tail. Then you want to cover the bottom of the doll in tin foil, then you want to cut a slit at the top of the tail and start working it around the doll, smoothing it out. Then you shape the tail however you like so the doll can sit / stand up. Then you want to carefully open the tin foil a little bit and slide out the doll.

## Detailing the Tail and Sculpting the Top

After baking you can add a few details. And here's the finished sculpted the tail. I baked it completely and then set it aside. For her top, I covered the doll in tin foil again and then cut out two shapes of polymer clay and fit these to the body. Once cooled, I paint them using alcohol ink in a gold color and then I seal it in with a bit of glaze.

## Beginning the Face Repaint

Before we start assembling the doll, we're gonna do the actual repaint. So take a bit of nail polish remover containing acetone and remove the factory paint of the face. Then I primed the face using the Mr. Super Clear spray before using my watercolor pencils, chalk pastel, and a bit of alcohol ink for the repaint.

I start by placing in the eyes, trying to get them as symmetrical as I can. She's not gonna have a defined iris since the whole eye is going to be one color. For the eyebrows, I'm sketching them out using a bit of chalk pastel, which I can erase easily before going over it with a pencil. To shade, I used a bit of chalk pastel in a green, which I usually don't do, but I wanted to give her skin sort of a greenish undertone. I used the metallic-looking alcohol ink to fill in the entire eye, but you could also use acrylic paint.

## Layering and Shading the Face

This is how far we got in the first layer. Then I sprayed the doll again with Mr. Super Clear spray and started working on top. I shade the corners of the eyes using black chalk pastel to make the eye look rounded. I deepened the general shading of the face with a dark brown pastel going on top of the green. Time for another spray.

## Final Details and Highlights

I used a watercolor effect of my pencil for more defined color. I used a light skin-color pencil for highlights, as I think the white would be too harsh. I use my white pencil on a wet brush to add the final white highlights of the eyes, and then she's ready for her final spray.

## Assembling the Doll

I'll add some gloss on the lips using a water-based glaze, but that's optional. Then we can start assembling the doll, starting by gluing on the chest pieces. I added a jump ring on top for a bit of additional detail and using a bit of copper wire to wrap around the wrist for cuffs.

Now for the tail, you're gonna need a bit of air dry clay to connect the doll to the tail and make it a smooth transition. It's important that it's air dry because you won't be able to bake the doll. Here I use a bit of water to smooth out the clay, and then I let it dry.

## Painting, Finishing Touches, and Final Reveal

Now we can paint the tail using acrylic paint. Sealing the paint with a bit of glaze, and then paint the wig. For the eyes of the snakes I used some yellow rhinestones, sealed in with glaze, and then we're ready to put it all together.

And here's our finished doll! So far, this was the biggest modification I've ever made on a doll and it was really fun. If you have any requests for future repaints, be it faes, creatures, monsters, characters, whatever, do leave them in the comments below, 'cause I really like to hear. Thank you guys so much for watching. Hit the like button if you enjoyed the video and I'll see you guys in a new one real soon. Bye.
